title: Coin Purse
body:
Goal: finish a CoinPurse class for a game. It must never let the coins go below zero.

  1. Open starter.py in Thonny.
  2. Finish add, can_afford and spend.
  3. Press Run. You should see:
You have 10 coins
Bought a potion for 5. Left: 5 coins
Not enough coins for a shield (12).
Bought a map for 3. Left: 2 coins
Found 7 coins! Now: 9 coins

Git practice: copy your finished file into Documents/git-quest and commit it with a helpful message.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Look at the three methods with a TODO: add, can_afford and spend. Notice that spend is built on top of can_afford. Fix can_afford first. Then compare your output with the README.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: self.coins is the number the purse remembers. Use if with a comparison like > or >= to check a number. In spend, call self.can_afford(price) rather than doing the math again. A return gives back True or False.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Use these shapes. In add, write if amount > ____: and then self.coins = self.coins + ____. In can_afford, write return self.coins ____ price. In spend, ask can_afford first. If it says yes, take the price away and give back True. If not, give back False.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.html: # Coin Purse - YOUR version # A CoinPurse object keeps track of the coins a player has in a game. # The class protects its number: coins can never go below zero. # Finish the TODOs, then press Run and see if it does what the README says. SHOP = {"potion": 5, "shield": 12, "map": 3} class CoinPurse: """Blueprint for a purse of game coins.""" def __init__(self, coins=0): self.coins = coins def add(self, amount): """Add coins. Ignore amounts of 0 or less.""" # TODO 1: only if amount is more than 0, add it to self.coins pass def can_afford(self, price): """Return True if there are enough coins to pay price.""" # TODO 2: return True when self.coins is at least price return False def spend(self, price): """Pay price if we can afford it. Return True if paid, False if not.""" # TODO 3: if self.can_afford(price): take price away and return True # otherwise return False return False def describe(self): return f"{self.coins} coins" if __name__ == "__main__": purse = CoinPurse(10) print("You have", purse.describe()) for item, price in SHOP.items(): if purse.spend(price): print(f"Bought a {item} for {price}. Left: {purse.describe()}") else: print(f"Not enough coins for a {item} ({price}).") purse.add(7) print("Found 7 coins! Now:", purse.describe())
